cards.explanation: The answer is Certainly not. Paul doesn't dance around it, friends. He says "Certainly not!" (Romans 6:15). Grace isn't a permission slip, and Paul shuts that idea down in two words.

The answer is the one you obey. Paul says "…you are slaves to the one you obey…" (Romans 6:16). Whoever you keep offering yourself to is the one in charge. It's not about a title on paper. It's about who you're actually listening to.

The answer is False. Paul lays out only two: "…slaves to sin leading to death, or to obedience leading to righteousness?" (Romans 6:16). There's no third door marked Nobody's The Boss, friends. I'd love that door too, but it's not in the text.
The answer is death. Paul says being "…slaves to sin…" leads "to death" (Romans 6:16). Every master has a destination, friends, and this one's a heavy one.

The answer is that they wholeheartedly obeyed the teaching. Paul says "…thanks be to God that, though you once were slaves to sin, you wholeheartedly obeyed the form of teaching to which you were committed." (Romans 6:17). Notice he thanks God. The whole moment is a thank-you, not a pat on the back for them.

The answer is True. Paul says, "You have been set free from sin and have become slaves to righteousness." (Romans 6:18). Free from one master, now serving another, friends. And this master is a good one.

The answer is the same parts they once gave to impurity. Paul says, "Just as you used to offer the parts of your body in slavery to impurity and to escalating wickedness, so now offer them in slavery to righteousness leading to holiness." (Romans 6:19). Same parts, new master. I like how practical that is, bakers.
The answer is ashamed. Paul asks about "…the things of which you are now ashamed?" (Romans 6:21). The word now matters, friends. Looking back, those things don't look so good anymore.

The answer is False. Before, "The outcome of those things is death." (Romans 6:21). Now, for those set free from sin and slaves to God, "…the outcome is eternal life." (Romans 6:22). Death on one side, eternal life on the other. That's a big difference, bakers.

The answer is gift. Paul says "…the gift of God is eternal life in Christ Jesus our Lord." (Romans 6:23). Wages are what you earn, but a gift is handed to you. Paul wants us to see that difference clearly, friends. Eternal life comes in Christ Jesus our Lord.
